scope: Certified Rust native lifecycle, direct target, shared portfolio, and bounded package shapes only.

matching.candidate_property: Exact set of active orders in stable monotonic sequence order.
matching.small_shape_policy: Use the same exact active-index scan; no unmeasured price-index threshold is enabled.
matching.same_phase_child_policy: Append newly activated children to the existing continuation queue after the captured priority snapshot.
matching.fallback: The certified generic lifecycle matcher remains the only static-order fallback.
not_supported: price-index priority replacing stable sequence priority

ownership.hot_state: OrderState contains only numeric lifecycle, quantity, price, timing, and relation fields.
ownership.cold_data: Public strings/provenance are adapted outside the Rust order arena from command/output data.
ownership.alias_index: ExternalOrderAliases is bidirectional and generation-safe through OrderHandle.
ownership.scratch: FullSession owns reusable matching_candidates and lifecycle_candidates; result_buffers reset can release their capacity.

workloads.contract: Direct target rebalance with Rust-owned accounting; no synthetic order lifecycle is claimed.
Exact stable-sequence lifecycle matching with reusable scratch and bounded alias cleanup.
Python decisions remain dynamic; Rust retains lifecycle/accounting and uses the same FullSession matcher.
Shared-account target admission preserves declared sequential, reduce-first, pro-rata, and all-or-none policies.
Atomic/best-effort package policies preserve committed-account and actual-fill hedge semantics.

decision_rules.promotion_rule: A shape is enabled only through its existing explicit contract and must retain independent financial parity evidence.
